rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule guards: a reader stuck on a pronoun/noun with no resolvable antecedent. Checked every chunk: chunk0 'the audit'/'the scoped task' (line 7) resolve via the session-artifacts carve-out (real prior M4 beat, confirmed against run-the-first-experiment.md:155 and trainer-modules.md:324/331 which name the audit this session ran); chunk1 'the two return markers' cashes out against chunk0's 'What you build' line 11; chunk2 'this commit'/'the branch name' continue chunk1's ask; chunk3 'The commit is local' continues chunk2; chunk4 'the scoped task we scoped earlier' is the same session-artifact carve-out; chunk5 'it runs' (heading) and 'it' (line 56) resolve to chunk4's just-sent task (immediate sequential continuation), 'The trace' (line 57) resolves under the session-artifact carve-out as the current run's own record, reinforced by chunk1's transcript-path beat. No never-named or vague-with-history referent found.

Harm: a callback that only resolves if you know which file precedes this one in delivery order. Scanned all 6 chunks for phrasing like 'the opening lecture said' / positional pointers to other files: none present. All callbacks are same-file sequential (rule 1's territory) or session-artifact references, not cross-file position pointers.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a 'the X you did' pointing at a beat that got cut in a rewrite, stranding the student. Checked chunk0's 'the audit' and 'the scoped task' (line 7) against the module's actual M4 sequence: `grep -rn 'the audit' curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/{run-the-first-experiment.md,trainer-modules.md}` returned run-the-first-experiment.md:155 ('the audit') and trainer-modules.md:324/331 naming the audit exercise immediately preceding this file in M4's flow. The referenced beat exists.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal beat in this file; every chunk is instruction + prompt, no predict/observe pairing.

Harm: a slide that says nothing standalone. Closest candidate is chunk3 ('Push it only if you want it off this laptop', lines 37-43) — shortest chunk — but it carries a self-carrying claim (the commit stays local by default, here's the optional push prompt), not a bare wait-state. All 6 chunks pass the size checker (`node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/exercises/set-the-markers-send-it-off.md` -> 'files: 1  slides: 5  oversized: 0'; chunk0 the title slide is outside that 5-slide count) confirming none is a stub.

Line closest to violating: chunk1 header 'Phase 1: Set the two return markers' (line 17) only executes ONE marker (the transcript path) within its own chunk boundary (lines 17-26); the second marker (the starting-point commit) is set in the next chunk, 'Pin the starting point'. Read as a phase-level umbrella header over the two immediately-following atomic headings (mirroring 'Phase 2: Send it off' as the umbrella for its single sub-beat), not a per-chunk literal-truth claim — the file's own two-tier heading structure (Phase N: <umbrella> then bare imperative sub-headings) makes this the deliberate shape, not a contradiction the chunk's content undercuts. Stays PASS, not REVISE.

Checked all sub-items across all chunks: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction; no anaphora/epistrophe triples; no self-grading superlative; no abstraction-noun stack; no empty-leg verb triplet. One number+retraction candidate: chunk5 line 56 'Past ten or so interventions, you have become the agent' — covered by the file's own maintainer block ('"Past ten or so, you've become the agent" stays — maintainer call 2026-08-02', citing the calibration-not-prescription boundary), an explicit maintainer attestation of this exact shape. Accept-with-note, no edit owed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk0 carries 5 bolded labels ('**Time:**', '**Session**', '**What you do:**', '**What you build:**', '**The point:**', lines 3-13) but each is a short (<=3 word) metadata handle marking a mode, structurally identical to the compendium's cleared 'Reading-list/menu slide' and LO-bullet exemptions (label bold, not sentence bold) — no bold spans a whole lead sentence. Chunks 1-5: no bold in body prose outside fenced prompt blocks (which are exempt).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Re-derived against the current heading, not the prior flag. Chunk5's heading now reads 'Nudge sparingly while it runs' (line 53) — verb-first imperative ('Nudge...') with an adverbial/temporal tail, matching this exercise file's established mood: every other body heading is imperative or a 'Phase N: <imperative>' label ('Set the two return markers', 'Pin the starting point', 'Push it only if you want it off this laptop', 'Send it off'). The prior flagged string was 'While it runs', a bare noun-phrase/prepositional heading with no steering verb — that shape is gone. The added adverb 'sparingly' does not convert this back into a declarative claim; it modifies the imperative verb, consistent with the maintainer's own stated intent (restraint-as-doctrine, not an over-promise of intervention). Checked the file's other 4 headings against the same rule: all imperative or Phase-label — no violations anywhere in the file.
